summary.text: First-named among the nine legitimate sons Electryon begot upon Anaxo at Mycenae — one of the brood who met the sons of Pterelaus in battle over the stolen cattle and perished in the mutual slaughter, leaving only the bastard Licymnius alive.

story.text: Apollodorus lists Stratobates at the head of Electryon's nine sons by Anaxo, daughter of Alcaeus: Stratobates, Gorgophonus, Phylonomus, Celaeneus, Amphimachus, Lysinomus, Chirimachus, Anactor, and Archelaus. Their sister Alcmena alone among the children would carry the line forward.

While Electryon reigned at Mycenae the sons of Pterelaus came with Taphians claiming Mestor's kingdom; when the king ignored them they drove off his cattle. Electryon's sons stood to the herds and in the fighting both bands fell — Apollodorus writes that of all Electryon's sons there survived only Licymnius, who was still young.
